raw_segments.text: To Madame de Grammott, come test to Gissen.
They scarce contain anything but amorous complaints,
expressed in a very rough style,
discovering the follies and outrages of a restless passion,
overgourged as it were, with jealousies, fears, and suspicions.
These contained in the edition of 1588-920 Sonnets of La Baudi, accompanied by a dedicatory
epistle to Madame de Gramont, the former which are referred to at the end of chap.
XXVIL, do not really belong to the book and are a very slight interest at this time,
the epistle is transferred to the correspondence.
The Sonnets with the letter were presumably sent some time after letters V at SAC.
Monteney seems to have had several copies written out to forward to friends or acquaintances.

raw_segments.text: Enter Sir Hugh Evans disguised with others as fairies.
Evans, Trib, Trib, Ferries, Cum, and remember your parts.
Be Pauled, I pray you follow me into the pit,
and when I give the watchwords do as I pid you.
